answer: Picture new identities as ships docking at a shared wharf: berthing is free, but leaving with cargo costs a bond that shrinks only as a slow river of witnessed deliveries builds behind the hull — a wake no copy can fake. A sybil fleet can clone hulls, but each berth still demands real work or real stake, and cargo per berth stays capped until the wake runs deep. Flooding the harbor with empty ships then costs more in fees than it earns, while honest newcomers still board zephyr-fast, paying the small entry price once and earning cheaper passage with every delivery completed.
